identity.headquarters: San Francisco Bay Area (Palo Alto), USA; Colossus supercomputer in Memphis, TN

value_chain.value_chain_position: xAI occupies a unique vertically integrated position spanning compute infrastructure, model training, and consumer/enterprise AI products. At the infrastructure layer, xAI operates Colossus, the world's largest AI supercomputer (555,000 NVIDIA GPUs, 2 GW capacity as of Jan 2026), built in Memphis, TN. This massive compute is used primarily for training and serving its own Grok foundation models, not sold as general-purpose cloud compute. Upstream, xAI depends on NVIDIA for GPUs (H100s) and Supermicro for server assembly. Downstream, it serves end users through the Grok chatbot (integrated into X/Twitter), Grok API for developers, and enterprise subscriptions. The Feb 2026 SpaceX-xAI merger ($1.25T combined valuation) further integrates xAI into a broader ecosystem spanning AI, connectivity (Starlink), and potentially orbital data centers.

key_products: Grok: AI chatbot and assistant integrated into the X platform, featuring real-time internet search, image generation (Aurora), and multi-modal reasoning. Available via free tier (limited), SuperGrok ($30/month), and SuperGrok Heavy (~$300/month). Grok 3 launched with frontier reasoning capabilities; Grok 5 expected Q1 2026. 2M token context window.

Grok API: Developer API offering Grok models (Grok 4.1, Grok 4.1 Fast, earlier versions) with competitive pricing from $0.20/M input tokens. Supports text, vision, and function calling. EU and US endpoints available. Caching mechanism offers 50-75% discounts on repeated prompts. Free credits up to $175/month for developers.

Colossus Supercomputer: The world's largest AI training cluster, currently at 555,000 NVIDIA GPUs across 2 GW capacity in Memphis, TN. Built in 122 days (initial 100K GPUs), expanded to 200K in 92 more days, with plans for 1M+ GPUs by late 2026. Primarily used for internal model training but represents a massive infrastructure asset valued at ~$18B in GPU purchases alone.

business.revenue_or_valuation: Valuation: $230B (Series E, Jan 2026); $250B implied in SpaceX merger (Feb 2026). Revenue: ~$300M estimated for full year 2025, exiting 2025 at ~$500M annualized run rate. Grok Q3 2025 revenue estimated at $88M. Projecting $2B+ revenue in 2026. Additionally secured U.S. DoD contracts with ceiling reportedly up to $200M-$300M.
business.annual_recurring_revenue_arr: $500M annualized run rate as of end 2025 (standalone, excluding X advertising revenue). Composed of SuperGrok consumer subscriptions, Grok Business/Enterprise plans (launched Dec 2025), and API usage. [uncertain]
business.funding_total_and_last_round: Total raised: ~$42B+ across all rounds. Series A: $135M (Nov 2023). Series B: $6B at $24B valuation (May 2024). Series C: $6B at $50B valuation (Dec 2024, investors: a16z, BlackRock, Fidelity, Sequoia, etc.). Debt+Equity: $10B (Jul 2025, incl. $5B debt via Morgan Stanley, $2B from SpaceX/Tesla). Series E: $20B at $230B valuation (Jan 2026, investors: Valor, Fidelity, QIA, MGX, NVIDIA $2B, Cisco). SpaceX acquired xAI in Feb 2026 at $250B valuation in all-stock deal ($1.25T combined).
business.business_model: Multi-stream: (1) Consumer subscriptions via SuperGrok ($30/mo) and SuperGrok Heavy (~$300/mo); (2) Enterprise subscriptions via Grok Business and Grok Enterprise (launched Dec 2025); (3) Usage-based API pricing (from $0.20/M tokens for fast models to $3/$15 per M tokens for Grok 4); (4) Government/defense contracts (DoD ceiling ~$200M-$300M); (5) Integration revenue via X platform (Grok embedded for X Premium subscribers). Targeting profitability by 2027.
business.burn_rate_and_runway: Approximately $1B/month burn rate, driven primarily by massive GPU infrastructure buildout ($18B in GPU purchases) and operational costs. Following SpaceX merger (Feb 2026) and $20B Series E, runway is extended through SpaceX's balance sheet and potential IPO (targeting up to $50B raise at $1.5T valuation in 2026).

openness.open_vs_closed_spectrum: Hybrid. Grok-1 open-sourced under Apache 2.0 (Mar 2024, weights only, no training code). Grok 2.5 released as open-weight under restrictive license (Aug 2025, commercial use restricted). Frontier models (Grok 3, Grok 4) are closed/API-only. Overall trajectory: earlier models open-sourced, newer frontier models kept proprietary.

startup_relevance.relevance_for_startups: xAI matters for entrepreneurs in several distinct ways: (1) API competition: Grok API pricing is highly competitive ($0.20/M tokens for fast models), with generous free credits ($175/month), making it an affordable alternative to OpenAI/Anthropic for startups building AI-powered products; (2) Real-time data advantage: Grok's integration with X/Twitter provides unique real-time social data access that other LLMs lack, valuable for startups in social listening, news analysis, or trend detection; (3) Infrastructure precedent: The Colossus build (100K GPUs in 122 days) demonstrates that massive AI infrastructure can be built at unprecedented speed, reshaping expectations for compute scaling timelines; (4) Vertical integration model: The Tesla-X-xAI-SpaceX ecosystem exemplifies extreme vertical integration in AI -- from energy (Tesla Megapack), to data (X platform), to compute (Colossus), to models (Grok), to distribution (X, Tesla vehicles) -- a case study in platform strategy; (5) Enterprise market entry: Grok Business/Enterprise plans (Dec 2025) signal xAI's push into B2B, creating partnership and integration opportunities for enterprise-focused startups; (6) Open-weight models: Grok-1 (Apache 2.0) and Grok 2.5 (restricted) offer options for startups wanting to self-host or fine-tune, though with limitations compared to Meta's Llama ecosystem; (7) Geopolitical context: As a US company with deep government ties (DoD contracts, Musk's political connections), xAI's trajectory illustrates how AI companies navigate government relationships and defense applications.
startup_relevance.accessibility: Highly accessible for developers. Grok API offers competitive per-token pricing starting at $0.20/M input tokens (Grok 4.1 Fast), up to $175/month in free credits, and EU endpoint availability (eu-west-1). Consumer access through X platform (free tier with limited Grok access, SuperGrok at $30/month). Enterprise plans available (Grok Business, Grok Enterprise) with GDPR/CCPA compliance and SOC 2 Type 2 certification. No dedicated startup program identified. Open-weight Grok-1 available for self-hosting. API documentation at docs.x.ai.
startup_relevance.primary_model_dependency: Self-sufficient. xAI develops Grok models internally using Colossus infrastructure. Depends on NVIDIA GPUs (H100) for compute hardware.

ecosystem.key_partnerships: NVIDIA: $2B strategic investment in Series E, primary GPU supplier (H100s) for Colossus. SpaceX: acquired xAI in Feb 2026, combined $1.25T entity, plans for orbital data centers. Tesla: $2B investment in xAI, supplies Megapack batteries for Colossus power, Grok integrated into Tesla vehicles. X (formerly Twitter): xAI acquired X Corp in Mar 2025 ($33B all-stock), X investors hold 25% of xAI, X platform serves as primary distribution channel and real-time data source. Supermicro: server assembly partner for Colossus. Cisco: strategic investor in Series E. Oracle: early cloud partnership for GPU access. Key financial investors: a16z, Sequoia, BlackRock, Fidelity, QIA, MGX.
ecosystem.competitive_moat: Unmatched compute scale: Colossus is the world's largest AI supercomputer (555K GPUs, 2 GW), with plans for 1M+ GPUs, giving xAI training capacity that only a handful of organizations can match. Unique data access: X platform integration provides real-time social media data unavailable to competitors, enabling differentiated training data and live information retrieval. Musk ecosystem synergies: Tesla (energy, vehicles, robotics), SpaceX (connectivity, orbital compute), and X (distribution, data) create a vertically integrated moat spanning hardware, energy, data, distribution, and applications. Speed of execution: demonstrated ability to build 100K GPU clusters in 122 days, significantly faster than typical data center timelines. Capital access: $42B+ raised in under 2 years, with SpaceX merger providing access to even larger capital pools.
ecosystem.data_moat_type: Proprietary training data / User feedback loop / Distribution

regulatory.regulatory_exposure: GPAI provider under EU AI Act for Grok models. xAI offers EU endpoint (eu-west-1) for data residency. Grok Business/Enterprise are GDPR and CCPA compliant with SOC 2 Type 2 certification. However, as a US company with deep ties to Elon Musk's political activities (DOGE involvement in US government), xAI faces heightened scrutiny in EU markets. The SpaceX merger may further complicate regulatory positioning given SpaceX's defense contracts and Starlink's geopolitical role. DoD contracts indicate significant US government entanglement that could create tensions with EU sovereignty requirements.
